is_anopheles.evidence: Adult mosquitoes were identified morphologically and molecularly using SINE200 as Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (p. 2-4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: TaqMan assays were used to genotype Vgsc-L1014F and Vgsc-L1014S (p. 3, 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 gives exact genotype counts (L1014F/L1014F, L1014F/L1014S, L1014S/L1014S) and allele counts for Lambaréné (N=60) and Zilé (N=56) (p. 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae were sampled from breeding sites in Lambaréné and Zilé, Moyen-Ogooué Province, Gabon, and reared to adults (p. 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical research paper reporting original susceptibility tests and kdr genotyping from field collections (p. 1-2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Lambaréné and Zilé in Moyen-Ogooué Province, Gabon (p. 2, Fig. 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections took place from November 2017 to February 2018 (p. 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The authors refer to their previous study in Zilé (ref 18), but describe these as specific larvae collections conducted from November 2017 to February 2018.

supplement.evidence: All genotype counts and frequencies are reported in the main text and Table 2.

assessment.summary: This study reports WHO susceptibility assays (deltamethrin, permethrin, DDT) and kdr genotyping (Vgsc-L1014F and L1014S) in Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected as larvae in Lambaréné and Zilé, Moyen-Ogooué Province, Gabon between November 2017 and February 2018. Genotype counts are clearly tabulated in Table 2 for both localities.
